title: Read-your-writes through an unsynchronized replica
pattern: A session writes an entity to its source of truth (primary node or system of record) and reads the same entity from an asynchronous replica or migration target before that target is known to include the write.
why_bad: Asynchronous replication introduces a non-zero propagation delay before writes on the primary are reflected on followers or migration targets [116]. Reading from the lagging target exposes stale or missing data, making the user's recently submitted update appear lost and violating the expected read-after-write (read-your-writes) consistency guarantee [117, 130, 191, 659].
detection: A write method call on a primary/source-of-truth client is followed, on the same execution path or within the same session (not necessarily adjacent), by a read method call for the same entity key on a different client that is an asynchronously updated replica or migration target of the first, without a replication-position or version barrier between them.
source: Martin Kleppmann, *Designing Data-Intensive Applications*, Chapter 5 (Replication Lag) / passages [116, 117, 130, 206]; Alex Petrov, *Database Internals*, Chapter 11 / passage [53]; Designing Data-Intensive Applications, Chapter 5, "Eventual consistency - Read-after-write consistency" [191, 659]
